topic.title: Incremental compact evidence beyond exchangeable joint histories
topic.question: Does combining the compact-statistics/grouped-history source with exchangeable_joint outperform both frozen source bests, especially exchangeable_joint, under the frozen information and training protocol with capacity, redundancy, and measured cost controlled?
topic.hypothesis: The current source inherits count/freshness evidence and match_groups; the other source supplies the stronger exchangeable_joint representation. Compact evidence may improve access to information beyond exchangeable_joint, but shared grouped-history ancestry could make the sources redundant. Predict an advantage over both frozen source bests that survives matched-capacity and duplicated-evidence controls and repetition. Failure to exceed exchangeable_joint, or an advantage reproduced by added capacity or duplicated evidence, would leave complementarity unsupported. Measure parameter count and training/inference cost against both sources; predictive gain alone does not establish efficiency or a mechanism.
